description:
Read every Notion page or comment that changed after `since` and names one of this workspace's own members — a person-valued property, an inline @mention in a page, or an @mention inside a comment. The match against a member comes only from Notion's own `<mention-user url="user://...">` tag: never a name, an email, or free text in the page's prose.

This tool makes no judgment: it does not decide whether a page asks the member to act, is informational, is noise, or is an echo of a comment Well itself posted. That triage is the caller's own job, using each row's `zone`, `excerpt` and the fact that the row exists at all (a comment line Well itself wrote still carries no `<mention-user>` tag unless it names someone, so a plain acknowledgement never appears here).

With no Notion connector live in this workspace, returns `connected: false` and reads nothing. Bounded at 25 changed pages per call, oldest changes first; `truncated: true` means either more pages changed than this call read, or a transient or connection failure (timeout, 5xx, rate limit, revoked grant) stopped the run partway through rather than skip the failed page. Either way, pass `cursor` as the next call's `since` and `cursor_note_id` as its `after_note_id` to keep going from the last page this call fully read, never re-reading what it covered and never skipping a page changed at the same instant.

A failure that belongs to the connection (a revoked or expired grant, a missing scope or capability, a 401, 402 or 403, or any other typed 4xx outside the two codes below) stops the run at once with `truncated: true` and the cursor unchanged, so no page is lost while the member reconnects. A page whose own request is settled as wrong — Notion's own `object_not_found` code with a typed 404 or 410, or its `validation_error` code with a typed 400, and only those two — is skipped immediately, with no retry: its id and `updated_at` are reported in `failed_pages`, the cursor advances past it, and the run keeps reading later pages. A caller sees a page in `failed_pages` when mentions on that page may be incomplete for this and every future run, until the page is shared back or re-created.

`dedup_key` is stable across runs for the same page/comment, zone and member: a caller uses it to never act on the same appearance twice.

after_note_id.description: The previous call's cursor_note_id, passed with its cursor as since: the read then also takes the pages changed at that same instant after this note.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

since.description: Only pages and comments that changed strictly after this ISO-8601 instant are read. Pass the workspace's own last-run watermark, never a guessed date.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_find_notion_mentions

comment_id.description: Set only when zone is comment.

excerpt.description: Up to 240 characters of the page or comment text around the mention.

member_id.description: The person_id of the Well member Notion's mention-user tag names.

property_names.description: Every Notion property's own JSON key (`Assignee`, `Created by`, a custom label, …) that names the member, in key order, when zone is properties; an empty array otherwise. A member named under more than one property gets every label here, never only the first — this tool reads no property type, so a caller judging whether any label names a real assignment reads the labels themselves, not a type this tool does not have.

provider_note_id.description: The Notion page's note id in this workspace.

self_mention.description: True when zone is comment and the comment's own author is the member it names: the member wrote it to themselves. False otherwise, and on a page or property zone.

connected.description: False when this workspace has no live Notion connector; every other field is then empty.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

cursor.description: Pass as the next call's `since` to continue past a truncated result.

cursor_note_id.description: Pass as the next call's `after_note_id`, with cursor as since. Null when there is no page to resume after.

failed_pages.description: Pages this run skipped because the provider answered with Notion's own object_not_found code on a typed 404/410, or validation_error code on a typed 400 — never any other failure, which stops the run instead. The cursor advances past each of these, so mentions on them may be incomplete for this and every future run.

provider_note_id.description: The Notion page's note id this run gave up on after one settled, page-attributable failure.

updated_at.description: The page's `updated_at` at the time this run gave up on it.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

title: Find notion mentions
